events.summary:
Oregon Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air Quality
Advisory until 2 PM PDT Monday.

For the Smoke Air Quality Advisory, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems.  Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

For additional information...please visit the Web site at
http://www.oregon.gov/DEQ

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Portions of north central North Carolina, including the
following counties, Stokes and Surry and southwest Virginia,
including the following county, Patrick.

* WHEN...Until 200 PM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 426 AM EDT, flooding continues as several creeks and
rivers remain well out of their banks due to runoff from
heavy rain earlier tonight.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Beaver Creek, Big Creek, Big Beaver Island Creek, Baker
Branch, Archies Creek and Ararat River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mount Airy, Fairview, Dobson, Pilot Mountain, Danbury,
Francisco and Sandy Ridge.
- For flooding safety information, please visit
http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Corrected timing information.

...SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 6 AM CHST
FRIDAY...

* WHAT...West winds 15 to 25 kt and seas 8 to 12 feet expected.
Gusts to 35 kt possible.

* WHERE...Guam Coastal Waters.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM ChST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Fresh to strong westerlies will continue
across Guam coastal waters, generating choppy seas hazardous to
small craft. Winds will peak in the first half of this week,
with a possibility of frequent gale-force gusts Monday and
Tuesday, which would necessitate a Gale Warning at that time.
Additionally, distant Typhoon Dolphin (12W) is generating a
long-period easterly swell that is moving through the Marianas,
which will gradually shift north over the next day or so, then
shift to the northwest. Meanwhile, the developing monsoon
pattern will lead to increasing southwesterly swell over the
coming days. These increasing swells and wind waves will build
combined seas to exceed 10 feet across the coastal waters,
maintaining hazardous sea conditions for much of this week.

events.summary:

* WHEN...From 6 AM Monday to 6 AM ChST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

generating choppy seas hazardous to small craft. Winds will peak
in the first half of this week, with a possibility of frequent
gale-force gusts Monday and Tuesday, which would necessitate a
Gale Warning at that time. Additionally, distant Typhoon Dolphin
(12W) is generating a long-period northeast to east swell that
is moving through the Marianas, which will gradually shift north
over the next day or so, then shift to the northwest.
Meanwhile, the developing monsoon pattern will lead to
increasing southwesterly swell over the coming days. These
increasing swells and wind waves will build combined seas to
exceed 10 feet across the coastal waters, maintaining hazardous
sea conditions for much of this week.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...FLASH FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 830 AM EDT THIS
MORNING FOR NORTHEASTERN SURRY COUNTY...

At 410 AM EDT, severe flooding continues as several creeks and
rivers remain well out of their banks due to runoff from heavy rain
earlier tonight. This resulted in numerous water rescues in the Mt.
Airy and Pilot Mountain areas earlier in the night. However, the
Ararat River at Mt. Airy crested near 29 feet at around 3 AM, and
water levels are now falling quickly. Water levels in Rutledge
Creek, Seed Cane Creek, Faulkner Creek, and Big Creek are likely
falling as well. Regardless, numerous roads remain flooded and
impassible, including East Pine Street, Riverside Drive, Westfield
Road, and Welcome Baptist Church Road. This remains a very dangerous
situation, as motorists may unknowingly drive into deep flood
waters, not realizing the flooding is there due to the darkness.

This is a FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for areas surrounding the towns of
Mt. Airy and Pilot Mountain. This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS
SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. Life
threatening flooding of low water crossings, small
creeks and streams, urban areas, highways, streets and
underpasses continues.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mount Airy...                      Flat Rock...
Pilot Mountain...                  Cana...
Woodville...                       Ararat...
Westfield...

events.summary:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 10 AM CDT /9 AM MDT/ THIS MORNING
TO 8 PM CDT /7 PM MDT/ THIS EVENING FOR MUCH OF WESTERN NORTH DAKOTA,
EXTENDING UNTIL 8 PM MDT MONDAY FOR SLOPE AND BOWMAN COUNTIES...

.Critical fire weather conditions are expected late this morning
through early this evening across much of western North Dakota. A
cold front will move into western North Dakota by early afternoon,
shifting winds from south to northwest around 20 mph with gusts up to
30 mph. Humidity is expected to fall as low as 10 to 15 percent this
afternoon. In the southwest corner of the state, humidity is only
projected to recover to around 45 percent overnight, then fall as low
as 20 percent on Monday as north winds increase to around 25 to 30
mph, with gusts as high as 40 mph. Therefore, the Red Flag Warning
remains in effect through early Monday evening for Slope and Bowman
Counties.

The National Weather Service in Bismarck ND has issued a Red Flag
Warning.

* AFFECTED AREA...Slope and Bowman Counties.

* TIMING...From 9 AM this morning to 8 PM MDT Monday.

* WINDS...For today, south winds shifting to the northwest around 20
mph with gusts up to 30 mph. For Monday, north winds around 25 to
30 mph with gusts up to 40 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...For today, as low as 10 to 15 percent. For
Monday, as low as 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
